mechanism: Both agents have anticholinergic properties; duloxetine has mild anticholinergic effects while scopolamine is a potent anticholinergic, creating additive central and peripheral anticholinergic toxicity.
action: Monitor for anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, cognitive impairment, tachycardia); consider alternative antiemetic if possible or use lowest effective scopolamine dose with patient education.
